in_hebrew.name: וילהלם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: וילהלם הוא שם שמקורו בשם הגרמני 'וילהלם', שמורכב מהמילים 'ויל' שפירושה 'חזק' או 'רצון' והמילה 'הלם' שפירושה 'קסדה' או 'מגן'. השם וילהלם ניתן לפרש כ'אלוהים הוא החזק שלי' או 'הוא שומר אותי'. השם וילהלם היה נפוץ בקרב מלכים ואצילים גרמנים וגם היה קשור לקתרקטת הצפונית של גרמניה.

in_greek.name: Βίλχελμ
in_greek.long_meaning: Βίλχελμ προέρχεται από το γερμανικό όνομα 'Βίλχελμ', που αποτελείται από τις λέξεις 'βίλ' που σημαίνει 'δύναμη' ή 'βούληση' και 'χέλμ' που σημαίνει 'κράνος' ή 'ασπίδα'. Το όνομα Βίλχελμ μπορεί να ερμηνευτεί ως 'Ο Θεός είναι η δύναμή μου' ή 'Είναι ο προστάτης μου'. Το όνομα Βίλχελμ ήταν συνηθισμένο ανάμεσα σε βασιλιάδες και ευγενείς Γερμάνους και συνδέθηκε επίσης με τη Βόρεια Θάλασσα της Γερμανίας.

in_latin.name: Wilhelm
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Wilhelm origine germanicum habet, componitur ex vocibus 'wil' quae significat 'voluntas' aut 'fortitudo' et 'helm' quae significat 'cassis' seu 'protector'. Nomen ergo Wilhelm interpretari potest 'Deus est mea fortitudo' vel 'Meus protector'. Hoc nomen inter reges et nobiles Germanos frequenter occurrebat, tum etiam cum mari boreali Germaniae coniunctum erat.

in_english.name: Wilhelm
in_english.long_meaning: The name Wilhelm originates from the Germanic name 'Wilhelm', composed of 'wil' meaning 'will' or 'resolute' and 'helm' meaning 'helmet' or 'protector'. It can be interpreted as 'resolute protector' or 'strong-willed warrior'. The name Wilhelm has been borne by several German kings and nobles throughout history, and is associated with strength, courage, and leadership. In Christian tradition, the name Wilhelm signifies a strong and steadfast follower of God.

data.cultural_impact: The name Wilhelm carries a rich historical and cultural significance. It has been popular in Germanic regions, and is known to have been borne by numerous kings, monarchs, and warriors throughout history. The name often represented strength, courage, and protection, qualities highly valued in the Germanic world.
data.spiritual_significance: Wilhelm's origin and etymology hints at a deep spiritual meaning. The name "Wilhelm" suggests a guardian, someone who protects, a potential savior. It is reminiscent of the idea of a 'warrior of God,' a strong and fearless protector of one's beliefs and community. The name evokes themes of protection, courage, and devotion, which can resonate spiritually with many.

historical_references.reference: Wilhelm I, also known as William the Great or William of Saxony, was a Holy Roman Emperor from 1493 to 1516. He was the last Emperor to be elected king of Germany by the seven electors, and he was also the first Habsburg Emperor. During his reign, he successfully defended the Holy Roman Empire against several threats, including the Ottoman Turks and the French King Louis XII.
historical_references.context: Holy Roman Empire, Ottoman Turks, French King Louis XII

historical_references.reference: Wilhelm Graf von Schaumburg-Lippe was a German nobleman and the ruling prince of Schaumburg-Lippe from 1893 to 1945. He is known for his strong anti-Nazi stance during the Nazi era, and he was one of the few German princes who refused to swear an oath of loyalty to Adolf Hitler. Wilhelm was also a member of the German Resistance, and he helped to shelter and protect refugees and dissidents.
historical_references.context: German nobility, German Resistance, Adolf Hitler
